problems.problem: Show that there is no arithmetic progression with three elements in the infinite geometric sequence $\{2^k\}_{k=0}^{\infty}.$
Compute $\det A$, where $A$ is the $n\times n$ skew-symmetric matrix with $A_{ii}=0$, $A_{ij}=a_{ij}$ for $i<j$, and $A_{ij}=-a_{ji}$ for $i>j$, and $n$ is odd.
problems.editorial_note: Matrix layout transcribed equivalently as entrywise definition; preserve odd n.

problems.problem: Let $[x]$ denote the integer part of $x$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left((\sqrt{3}+1)^n-[(\sqrt{3}+1)^n]\right).$
Let $f$ be an even, twice continuously differentiable function such that $f''(0)\neq0$. Prove that $f$ has an extremum at $x=0$.

review_note: Four original Category I questions transcribed from organizer's 1991 one-page original. The archive's Category II original question PDF was not verified, so this year must not be presented as a complete two-category edition.
